blocks: A short set of observations and aphoristic statements by Person/Steve Reich, written in New Mexico in the summer of 1968 and first published in the catalogue to the exhibition Anti-Illusion: Procedures/Materials at the Whitney Museum of American Art in 1969.

Reich writes about pieces of music that are themselves processes, which should be audible and should happen extremely gradually. He contrasts them with Person/John Cage's chance procedures and with serial music, where the process can't be heard in the sounding music.
Reprinted in Reich's Person/Steve Reich/Book/02/Writings on Music, 1965-2000 (Oxford University Press, 2002), pp. 34–36. The whole book is also in Reader: Writings on Music, 1965–2000.
A friend sent the book pointing to this essay for discussion, along with hecanjog/Process Music Citations.

The phrase "no room for improvisation" is Christensen's paraphrase of Reich (2003), quoted in Erik Schoster's paper Where do you place agency in a process-based music system. Reich's own sentence is the one above.
